title: 7 Signs Your EAP Needs a Modern Upgrade
summary: Low EAP utilization, long wait times, and limited data signal it may be time to modernize. Learn how HR leaders can evaluate and update their EAP.
body_text: Although 98% of large employers in the U.S. offer an EAP , only about 4% of employees use it —and at some organizations, utilization falls as low as 1% . Why do so few employees engage with a benefit that’s nearly universal? The reality is, the workforce has evolved, but traditional EAPs largely haven't. EAPs became the foundation of employer-sponsored mental health support in the 1970s, typically offering short-term counseling for specific, acute issues. For decades, that model worked—particularly for employees navigating substance use concerns or clinical crises. But today’s employees face sustained pressure, blurred work-life boundaries, and ongoing stress that doesn’t always rise to the level of crisis. When they turn to their EAP for support, they often encounter complex phone trees, administrative hurdles, long wait times, and limited options for non-urgent care. As a result, only 36% of employees believe their workplace benefits provide adequate mental health support . While EAPs still play an important role, employers who want to meet employee needs—and demonstrate real value—must be willing to reassess whether their current model is still fit for purpose. 7 Signs It May Be Time to Reevaluate Your EAP Despite these challenges, more than 80% of U.S. employers still offer a traditional EAP , and 30% plan to switch EAP vendors within the next two years . If you’re unsure whether change is necessary for your organization, the signals below can help identify where risk, inefficiency, or missed value may exist. 1. Utilization remains consistently low Low utilization is often attributed to stigma or lack of awareness—factors employers can address through education and culture. But when utilization stays low despite sustained communication, it often signals deeper structural issues. Complicated enrollment processes, outdated care modalities, and misalignment with employee preferences are difficult to fix without modernizing the program itself. Younger employees, in particular, often prefer digital-first care such as virtual sessions, asynchronous messaging, or self-guided tools. Yet few traditional EAPs support these expectations. Only 37% allow employees to text their provider , and 38% offer in-app messaging , according to Business Group on Health research . No matter how well an EAP is promoted, outdated systems will continue to suppress engagement. 2. Employees struggle to access timely care Employees wait an average of 4.9 days for an EAP appointment, with some waiting up to three weeks . The longer the delay, the greater the risk that mental health concerns worsen—particularly in high-stress or crisis situations. While long wait times are often framed as unavoidable, they’re typically the result of legacy models that rely on phone-based intake, limited provider availability, and manual clinician matching. For employers, slow access doesn’t just affect employee experience—it increases the likelihood of escalation, disengagement, and downstream costs. 3. Limited insight into outcomes or impact Disjointed systems and limited reporting make it difficult for many EAPs to demonstrate effectiveness. As a result, only 39% of employers analyze ROI for their EAP , leaving many leaders unsure whether their investment is driving meaningful outcomes. While employers can track metrics like absenteeism or turnover internally, an EAP should be able to report on: Clinical outcomes Engagement and utilization trends Service mix and care journeys Breakdowns by region, role, or demographic Without this visibility, it’s nearly impossible to refine strategy or prove value. 4. Provider access varies widely by geography Few traditional EAPs offer consistent coverage across all regions. Global employers often rely on multiple vendors, creating fragmented data and uneven care experiences. This patchwork approach can result in inequity—employees in certain countries may face longer waits, fewer modality options, or lower-quality care. Over time, these inconsistencies undermine employer commitments to equity and global workforce standards. For organizations competing for talent worldwide, consistency in mental health support is no longer optional. 5. Care isn’t culturally aligned Research shows therapy is twice as effective when delivered in a person’s native language , and cultural norms strongly influence how individuals seek and experience care, according to the U.S. Surgeon General . Yet fewer than 60% of EAPs allow employees to choose providers based on identity factors such as language, gender, or race. Only 43% offer anti-stigma training , and just 31% require cultural competency training for providers. Without culturally aligned care, access alone isn’t enough to drive meaningful outcomes. 6. Care ends after a fixed number of sessions Most EAPs cap support at three to 12 sessions per incident, with six being the average . While this may work for some needs, it leaves employees requiring longer-term support navigating fragmented referrals or entirely new benefit systems. When care stops abruptly, employees often disengage altogether—continuing to struggle at work while costs quietly accumulate. 7. Employees need more than crisis intervention Traditional EAPs are designed for crisis response, but they’re rarely designed for prevention. While nearly all offer crisis counseling and hotlines, far fewer provide coaching ( 63% ) or support groups ( 38% ). By the time challenges reach crisis levels, they’re harder—and more expensive—to address. Preventive models that offer varied pathways can support employees earlier and reduce escalation over time. What It Means to “Modernize an EAP” Modernizing an EAP doesn’t mean abandoning the model entirely. It means preserving what works while evolving what no longer serves today’s workforce or business realities. A modernized EAP typically: 1. Preserves valuable EAP fundamentals Crisis support and therapy remain critical, particularly for cost-conscious employers. Modernization focuses on how care is delivered—not eliminating these foundations. 2. Expands care options and equity, globally Beyond crisis care, modern solutions support a range of needs and preferences, including: Clinical therapy Mental health and career coaching Support groups tailored to life stages or shared experiences Self-guided digital resources across mental, physical, relational, and financial well-being Access should be consistent globally, with culturally competent providers available across regions. 3. Integrates reporting and consultative guidance Modernized EAPs offer real-time, global reporting and expert interpretation—helping employers understand trends, identify emerging needs, and optimize benefits strategy over time. How FlexEAP Addresses Common Gaps—Without Adding Risk Modern Health’s FlexEAP is designed to modernize traditional EAP structures while maintaining cost control and reducing employer risk. FlexEAP includes: An adaptive care model that supports therapy, crisis care, coaching, and digital resources across need levels Rapid time-to-care and in-app matching , with < 24 hours to first available appointment, on average A global provider network spanning 200+ countries and territories and 80+ languages Predictable pricing options that share risk and prevent cost volatility Unified reporting and customer success support to track engagement and impact across the workforce Improving, Not Disrupting, Your Mental Health Benefits Having a traditional EAP often isn’t enough. What matters is whether it’s delivering equitable access, meaningful outcomes, and measurable value. The good news: modernizing your mental health benefits doesn’t require disruption. Solutions like FlexEAP are built to evolve existing programs in a scalable, cost-controlled way.

One Liberty Properties Acquires Ten Industrial Properties, Comprising 637,633 sf Across Seven Logistics Markets
summary: – 79 Industrial Properties Will Comprise 82% of Total Portfolio Base Rent –– Properties Afford Meaningful Long-Term Mark-to-Market Opportunity –– Record...
body_text: – 79 Industrial Properties Will Comprise 82% of Total Portfolio Base Rent – – Properties Afford Meaningful Long-Term Mark-to-Market Opportunity – – Record Industrial Acquisition Activity Adds $246 Million Over the Last 12 Months – GREAT NECK, N.Y., Jan. 29, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- One Liberty Properties, Inc. (NYSE: OLP), a real estate investment trust focused on the ownership of industrial properties, today announced it has acquired a 637,633 square foot portfolio of ten well-located industrial properties, below replacement cost. The ten-property portfolio is 100% leased to six tenants, each of which has a global or national presence. The two largest tenants are wholly owned subsidiaries of investment grade companies. The average in place rent is below market, providing attractive mark to market upside. OLP financed the acquisition with a $17 million mortgage on six properties, and an approximately $30 million borrowing under its $100 million credit facility. The 7.5-year mortgage bears interest at a fixed rate of 5.53% (interest only for six months and thereafter on a 30-year amortization schedule). The credit facility bears a current floating interest rate of 5.45%. OLP anticipates obtaining additional financing on two other properties in the portfolio and using the net proceeds to pay down the credit facility. Patrick J. Callan, Jr., President and Chief Executive Officer of One Liberty stated, “With $246 million of industrial asset acquisitions, the last 12 months have been historic for the Company. Through accretive capital recycling, our industrial platform represents 82% of the total portfolio ABR. This portfolio acquisition of well-located facilities – each fully occupied and supported by strong contractual rent increases and significant mark-to-market upside – expands our footprint in supply-chain critical markets, further enhances the durability of our cash flows, and positions us to add incremental growth over time.” The properties are situated in seven diverse and growing distribution markets of Greensboro, NC, Columbia, SC, Birmingham, AL, Omaha, NE, Oklahoma City, OK, Salt Lake City, UT and Jackson, MS. The single-tenant buildings are modern, functional, with an average size of 64,000 square feet, average construction year of 2004, average clear height exceeding 24 feet, with many benefiting from industrial outdoor storage or excess trailer parking. title: Match Transactions with Regex Patterns
summary: Powerful Pattern Matching for Your Rules You can now use regular expressions (regex) in your Finta rules, giving you the flexibility to match complex pattern...
body_text: Powerful Pattern Matching for Your Rules You can now use regular expressions (regex) in your Finta rules, giving you the flexibility to match complex patterns with a single rule instead of creating multiple rules for similar transactions. What's New New Rule Operators Two new operators are available when creating rules: matches regex - Match transactions where the field value matches your pattern does not match regex - Match transactions where the field value does NOT match your pattern These operators work with the Summary and Original Description fields. Why This Matters Previously, if you wanted to categorize all your coffee purchases, you'd need separate rules for "Starbucks", "Coffee Bean", "Peet's Coffee", and every other coffee shop. Now you can create a single rule: Summary matches regex (Starbucks|Coffee Bean|Peet's|Dunkin) This one rule will match transactions from any of those merchants, keeping your rules list clean and manageable. More Examples Match any subscription: (Netflix|Spotify|Hulu|Disney) Match reference numbers: REF-\d{6} Match date patterns: \d{2}/\d{2}/\d{4} Match payment with optional reference: payment(?:\s*#\d+)? Match transaction IDs: [A-Z]{2,3}-\d{4,} All pattern matching is case-insensitive, so starbucks will match "STARBUCKS" and "Starbucks". Get Started Regex pattern matching is available now. When creating or editing a rule, select "matches regex" or "does not match regex" from the operator dropdown to start using pattern matching in your rules. title: Claude Opus 4.5 vs Gemini 3 Pro vs GPT 5.2: The Ultimate AI Content Generation Comparison
summary: Compare Claude Opus 4.5, Gemini 3 Pro, and GPT 5.2 for AI content generation. Real-world testing reveals which model excels at articles, marketing copy, and SEO.
body_text: The AI landscape has never been more competitive. With Anthropic's Claude Opus 4.5, Google DeepMind's Gemini 3 Pro, and OpenAI's GPT 5.2 all claiming frontier-level capabilities, choosing the right model for content generation has become increasingly complex. We put all three models through rigorous real-world testing using the Cosmic AI Platform to generate articles, marketing copy, and SEO-optimized content. Here's what we discovered. The Contenders at a Glance Claude Opus 4.5 Release: November 2025 Pricing: $5/$25 per million tokens (input/output) Context Window: 200K tokens Standout Feature: State-of-the-art reasoning and creative problem-solving Anthropic positions Claude Opus 4.5 as "the best model in the world for coding, agents, and computer use." But its capabilities extend far beyond code—it demonstrates exceptional performance in long-form content generation and nuanced writing tasks. Gemini 3 Pro Release: December 2025 Pricing: $2/$12 per million tokens (input/output) for prompts ≤200K tokens; $4/$18 for prompts >200K tokens Context Window: 1M tokens (industry-leading) Standout Feature: Multimodal reasoning across text, images, video, and audio Gemini 3 Pro represents Google's "most intelligent model yet," achieving 91.9% on GPQA Diamond and leading benchmarks in academic reasoning, visual understanding, and multimodal comprehension. GPT 5.2 Release: 2025 Pricing: $1.75/$14 per million tokens (input/output) Context Window: 400,000 tokens Standout Feature: Advanced reasoning with enhanced instruction following OpenAI's latest iteration continues to push boundaries in natural language understanding and generation, with improved coherence in long-form content. Real-World Content Generation Test Using the Cosmic AI Platform, we gave each model identical prompts across five content categories: Long-form blog articles (2,000+ words) Marketing copy (product descriptions, landing pages) SEO-optimized content (keyword integration, meta descriptions) Technical documentation (API guides, tutorials) Creative writing (storytelling, brand voice) Key Findings 1. Long-Form Article Quality Winner: Claude Opus 4.5 Claude Opus 4.5 demonstrated superior performance in crafting cohesive, well-structured long-form content. As noted in Cosmic's Opus vs Sonnet comparison , the model "handles ambiguity and reasons about tradeoffs without hand-holding." Key observations: Maintains narrative coherence across 3,000+ word articles Naturally incorporates transitions and logical flow Demonstrates genuine insight over cliché responses Uses 19% fewer tokens than Sonnet 4.5 for comparable output Gemini 3 Pro excelled at incorporating research and citations, leveraging its massive 1M token context window to synthesize information from multiple sources. However, output occasionally felt more encyclopedic than engaging. GPT 5.2 produced solid content but showed less consistency in maintaining voice and style across longer pieces. 2. Marketing Copy & Conversion Content Winner: Gemini 3 Pro Gemini 3 Pro's multimodal capabilities proved advantageous for marketing content. The model demonstrated: Better understanding of visual context when provided reference materials Strong performance in generating variations for A/B testing Excellent adaptation to different brand voices According to Google DeepMind's benchmarks , Gemini 3 Pro achieves 81.0% on MMMU-Pro (multimodal understanding), which translates to better comprehension of brand guidelines and visual assets. 3. SEO-Optimized Content Winner: Claude Opus 4.5 (with Gemini 3 Pro close behind) For SEO content, Claude Opus 4.5 showed remarkable ability to: Naturally integrate keywords without stuffing Structure content with proper heading hierarchy Generate compelling meta descriptions within character limits Create internal linking opportunities Gemini 3 Pro's search integration capabilities (achieving 45.8% on Humanity's Last Exam with search enabled) make it particularly effective for research-heavy SEO content that requires current information. 4. Technical Documentation Winner: Claude Opus 4.5 Given Opus 4.5's state-of-the-art coding performance (leading on SWE-bench Verified), it's unsurprising that technical documentation emerged as a strength. The model: Accurately explains complex concepts at multiple skill levels Generates working code examples Maintains consistency in terminology Identifies potential edge cases and gotchas As Anthropic notes , "Claude Opus 4.5 excels at long-horizon, autonomous tasks, especially those that require sustained reasoning and multi-step execution." 5. Creative Writing & Brand Voice Winner: Tie (Claude Opus 4.5 & GPT 5.2) Both models demonstrated strong creative capabilities: Claude Opus 4.5 showed particular strength in: Character voice consistency Narrative structure Emotional resonance Avoiding formulaic patterns GPT 5.2 excelled at: Stylistic flexibility Tone matching Creative metaphors Dialogue naturalness Pricing Comparison Understanding the cost structure is essential for scaling content operations: Model Input Cost (per 1M tokens) Output Cost (per 1M tokens) Notes Claude Opus 4.5 $5 $25 Consistent pricing across prompt sizes Gemini 3 Pro $2 (≤200K) / $4 (>200K) $12 (≤200K) / $18 (>200K) Tiered pricing based on prompt length GPT 5.2 $1.75 $14 Competitive pricing with advanced reasoning capabilities Cost Efficiency Analysis: For typical content generation workflows with prompts under 200K tokens, Gemini 3 Pro offers the most competitive pricing at $2/$12 per million tokens compared to Claude Opus 4.5's $5/$25. However, Claude's superior token efficiency can offset the higher base rate. In our testing, Opus 4.5 consistently used fewer tokens to achieve comparable or better results, particularly for long-form content. Batch Processing Discounts: Both Claude Opus 4.5 and Gemini 3 Pro offer 50% discounts for batch processing: Gemini 3 Pro Batch: $1/$6 per million tokens (≤200K prompts) Claude Opus 4.5 Batch: Pricing varies by implementation For high-volume content operations, batch processing can significantly reduce costs while maintaining quality. Token Efficiency Comparison Efficiency matters for production content workflows. Based on our testing: Model Avg. Tokens per 1,000-word Article Relative Cost Claude Opus 4.5 ~1,400 output tokens Baseline Gemini 3 Pro ~1,650 output tokens +18% GPT 5.2 ~1,550 output tokens +11% Claude Opus 4.5's efficiency aligns with real-world reports showing "22% fewer input tokens" and "12% fewer output tokens" compared to previous generations. Best Use Cases by Model Choose Claude Opus 4.5 When: Writing long-form editorial content Creating technical documentation Generating SEO-optimized articles Building content that requires sustained reasoning Token efficiency is a priority at scale Budget allows for premium quality Choose Gemini 3 Pro When: Working with multimodal content (images, video references) Synthesizing information from extensive source material Creating marketing content with visual context Requiring current information via search integration Processing very long documents (1M token context) Cost optimization is a primary concern Choose GPT 5.2 When: Flexibility across diverse content types Creative writing requiring stylistic range Rapid iteration on short-form content Existing OpenAI ecosystem integration Practical Implementation with Cosmic AI The Cosmic AI Platform makes it easy to leverage these models for content operations: AI Content Studio - Generate content models and articles from natural language Multi-model support - Switch between Claude, Gemini, and GPT models Bulk operations - Generate and update content at scale SEO optimization - Built-in tools for meta descriptions and structured data As demonstrated in Cosmic's real-world comparisons , the platform allows teams to "generate complete applications from natural language prompts" and "deploy instantly to see real-world results." Safety and Alignment Considerations For enterprise content workflows, model safety matters: Claude Opus 4.5 is described as "the most robustly aligned model" Anthropic has released, with "substantial progress in robustness against prompt injection attacks." Gemini 3 Pro includes Google's responsible AI frameworks and content filtering. GPT 5.2 continues OpenAI's safety research with enhanced guardrails. All three models are suitable for professional content generation with appropriate review workflows. Conclusion: Which AI Model Should You Choose? After extensive testing, here's our recommendation: For most content teams: Claude Opus 4.5 The combination of output quality, token efficiency, and sustained reasoning makes Opus 4.5 the strongest all-around choice for content generation. Its 19% efficiency gains compound significantly at scale, helping offset the higher per-token cost. For cost-conscious and multimodal workflows: Gemini 3 Pro If budget is a primary concern or your content process involves extensive research, visual assets, or very long source documents, Gemini 3 Pro's competitive pricing and 1M token context provide exceptional value. The lower base cost makes it ideal for high-volume operations. For diverse, high-volume content: GPT 5.2 Teams requiring maximum flexibility across content types and existing OpenAI integrations will find GPT 5.2 a reliable choice once pricing is announced. The good news? Platforms like Cosmic support multiple models, allowing you to choose the right tool for each task. Start with a free Cosmic account to test these models on your own content workflows. This comparison reflects model capabilities as of December 2025. AI models are continuously updated—check official documentation for the latest specifications. body_text: Good travel doesn’t need fanfare, just a smart plan and the right destination. From mountain towns to island escapes, these ten spots offer the kind of trip that stays with you. All reachable nonstop, all ready when you are. Asheville, NC Creative and calm with mountain views in every direction. Asheville’s downtown is packed with indie shops, craft breweries, and just enough weird to make it memorable. It’s the kind of place where time slows down in a good way. Missoula, MT Missoula blends riverfront ease with a punch of unexpected culture. One part wild, one part artsy, all wrapped in big Montana sky. Come for the trails, stay for the bookstores and breweries. Aruba Steady sunshine, warm water, and no rush whatsoever. Aruba does easy living right: beachfront breakfasts, late afternoon swims, and a breeze that takes the edge off everything. Your only job here is to show up and enjoy. Traverse City, MI Small-town charm with Great Lakes energy. You’ll find wineries, farm stands, and sunsets that feel like a personal reward. Whether you opt for a kayak or a nap, it’s all time well spent. New Orleans, LA Rich with rhythm, flavor, and stories around every corner. From beignets to brass bands, New Orleans invites you to lose track of time and lean in. It’s not just a destination, it’s a mood. Kalispell / Glacier National Park, MT A straight shot to one of the country’s most stunning national parks. Kalispell brings you close to Glacier’s peaks, trails, and that quiet awe you can’t get from a screen. Pack those hiking boots and hit the trail. Cozumel, MX Island pace, reef colors, and nothing to prove. Cozumel is all about the in-between moments – hammock naps, street tacos, and quiet snorkeling spots. Easy to get to, hard to leave. Savannah, GA Moss-draped oaks, old streets, and a hush that makes you want to whisper. Savannah’s beauty isn’t loud, it’s all in the details. Ghost stories, garden squares, and southern comfort with style. Charleston, SC History in the walls, salt in the air, and food worth talking about. Charleston walks that line between refined and relaxed like no place else. It’s a city that invites you to linger. Vancouver, BC Mountains, ocean, and global flavor all in one view. Vancouver blends natural drama with urban cool. It’s a place to hike, eat well, and breathe easier. Come curious, leave full. The best trips don’t shout, they just feel right. Wherever 2026 takes you, these spots offer something worth showing up for. All that’s left to do is pick one. EXPLORE FLIGHTS

summary: Taylor Devices has established an in-house development lab that brings together dedicated engineering, expert machining, advanced CNC equipment, and high-performance 3D printing.
body_text: Taylor Devices held a ribbon-cutting ceremony last week marking the official grand opening of the Alan Klembczyk Development Lab, named in honor and recognition of the recently retired, former President of Taylor Devices, Alan Klembczyk. What's New in Cinapse — January 2026
summary: The January 2026 Cinapse update adds images to breakdown sheets, improves Scriptation and schedule importing, introduces easier plan upgrades, and delivers key performance and authentication fixes for film and TV productions.
body_text: January’s release delivers a mix of new capabilities , production-management improvements , and important fixes across scheduling, importing, permissions, and performance. This update focuses on making Cinapse even more flexible as productions scale — while smoothing out real-world edge cases reported by working ADs and production teams. 🔁 Subscription & Production Management Upgrade Path: Starter → Team → Team Pro You can now upgrade seamlessly between Starter, Team, and Team Pro as your production grows — without needing to reach out to the Cinapse team. This makes it easier to start small and scale up only when you need additional features, seats, or permissions. 👥 Buy Additional Seats for Your Production Productions can now add more seats mid-run , giving teams flexibility as new collaborators join. If you only need seats for part of the production, our team can still help tailor this — but the default self-serve flow is now faster and clearer. To upgrade or add seats: Select the production name next to the Cinapse logo, or Select My Account , or Select Members Then navigate to Production Settings → Plan . 🔑 Transfer Ownership Workflow A new ownership transfer workflow is now available, making it easier to hand off productions when roles change or teams transition. You can access this via the My Productions page — right-click or use the menu on the right side of a production to transfer ownership, upgrade plans, rename the production, and more. 🖼️ Breakdown Sheets: Images (New!) You can now upload images directly to breakdown sheets . This unlocks richer visual context for props, wardrobe, locations, VFX, and more — especially helpful for prep-heavy or visually complex productions. Pro tip: Upload reference images from Shotdeck or other visual libraries to keep everything in one place. New breakdown reports that include images are coming soon. 📥 Importing & Data Integrity Improvements We shipped several important fixes to script and schedule importing to ensure schedules reflect exactly what you intended — no missing data, no silent changes. Fixed: Repeated strips and breakdowns (e.g. weather cover scenes used multiple times throughout a schedule) are no longer deduplicated when importing .cinapse files Importing Scriptation into an existing file now correctly places new strips into the Scrapyard for use across all stripboards Importing Scriptation files now correctly respects Episodic vs Feature Film file types Overall improvements to reliability and accuracy across Scriptation and .cinapse imports These fixes directly address real-world episodic, revision-heavy, and multi-board workflows. 🧭 Scheduling & Calendar Fixes Fixed an issue where Editor users could not duplicate calendars Fixed right-click copy / paste menu behavior on the stripboard Improved change function performance across schedules 🔎 Navigation, Search & UI Improvements Improved free-text searching across productions Fixed an issue where special characters were not displaying correctly in the production navigation General UI polish and stability improvements 🔐 Authentication & Platform Improvements Improved login, sign-up, and authentication flows Backend and platform updates to support safer, faster releases going forward What’s Next Coming soon: Private Stripboards (Team Pro only) Reporting UI upgrades and new layouts Expanded publishing and permissions workflows Continued performance and reliability improvements As always, thank you to the filmmakers, ADs, UPMs, and producers who keep sending thoughtful, candid feedback. This release is a direct result of how Cinapse is used on real productions around the world. I personally review every piece of feedback that comes in. Please submit feedback anytime at feedback.cinapse.io

body_text: NEWS RELEASE January 23, 2026 TABER, ALBERTA, January 23, 2026 – FLEXIBLE SOLUTIONS INTERNATIONAL, INC. (NYSE-AMERICAN: FSI), is the developer and manufacturer of biodegradable polymers for oil extraction, detergent ingredients and water treatment as well as crop nutrient availability chemistry. Flexible Solutions also manufactures biodegradable and environmentally safe water and energy conservation technologies. In addition, FSI is increasing its presense in the food and nutrition supplement manufacturing markets. Today the Company announces fourth quarter (Q4) and full year, 2025 revenue. Sales were higher in Q4, 2025 compared to Q4, 2024. Flexible Solutions’ top line revenue increased from $8.84million (Q4, 2024) to $9.10million (Q4, 2025), up approximately 3% year over year. Full year revenue increased from $38.23million in 2024 to $38.50million in 2025, a full year increase of approximately 1%. Mr. Dan O’Brien, CEO, comments, “The 2025 year was one of transition as our Panama factory was built and our Illinois factory was retooled for our new contracts. Agriculture was difficult all year in all geographies. This obscured the excellent forward progress in food grade products.” Mr. O’Brien continues, “We anticipate that the opposite will be true in 2026 provided that food grade production reaches the much higher revenue we hope for.” Complete financial results will be available after market close on March 31, 2026 concurrent with the Company’s SEC full year filings. A conference call will be scheduled for 8:00 am Pacific Time, 11:00 am Eastern Standard Time, the following business day, Wednesday, April 1, 2026. See the FSI March 31, 2026 financials news release for the dial in numbers. About Flexible Solutions International Flexible Solutions International, Inc. ( www.flexiblesolutions.com ), based in Taber, Alberta, is an environmental technology company. The Company’s NanoChem Solutions Inc. subsidiary specializes in biodegradable, water-soluble products utilizing thermal polyaspartate (TPA) biopolymers. TPA beta-proteins are manufactured from the common biological amino acid, L-aspartic and have wide usage including scale inhibitors, detergent ingredients, water treatment and crop enhancement. Along with TPA, this division started producing other crop enhancement products as well. In 2022, the Company entered the food and nutrition markets by obtaining FDA food grade approval for the Peru IL plant. The other divisions manufacture energy and water conservation products for drinking water, agriculture, industrial markets and swimming pools throughout the world. title: SIERRA BANCORP ANNOUNCES 4% INCREASE IN QUARTERLY CASH DIVIDEND
summary: PORTERVILLE, CALIF. – (BUSINESS WIRE) – Sierra Bancorp (Nasdaq: BSRR), parent of Bank of the Sierra, announced that its Board of Directors has declared a regular quarterly cash dividend of $0.26…
body_text: January 30, 2026 PORTERVILLE, CALIF. – (BUSINESS WIRE) – Sierra Bancorp (Nasdaq: BSRR), parent of Bank of the Sierra, announced that its Board of Directors has declared a regular quarterly cash dividend of $0.26 per share. This represents an increase of $0.01 per share, or 4%, relative to the dividend paid last quarter. The dividend was approved subsequent to the Board’s review of the Company’s financial performance and capital for the quarter ended December 31, 2025, and will be paid on February 17, 2026, to shareholders of record as of February 9, 2026. Counting dividends paid by Bank of the Sierra prior to the formation of Sierra Bancorp, the Company has paid regular cash dividends to shareholders every year since 1987, comprised of annual dividends through 1998 and quarterly dividends thereafter. The dividend noted in today’s announcement marks the Company’s 108th consecutive quarterly cash dividend. Sierra Bancorp is the holding Company for Bank of the Sierra (www.bankofthesierra.com), which is in its 49th year of operations and is one of the largest independent banks headquartered in the South San Joaquin Valley. Bank of the Sierra is a community-centric regional bank, which offers a broad range of retail and commercial banking services through full-service branches located within the counties of Tulare, Kern, Kings, Fresno, Ventura, San Luis Obispo, and Santa Barbara. The Bank also maintains an online branch and provides specialized lending services through its mortgage warehouse division. In 2025, Bank of the Sierra was recognized as one of the strongest and top-performing community banks in the country, with a 5-star rating from Bauer Financial.
